newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina gov urges $600 million cuts.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina gov urges $600 million cuts.

text.p: North Carolina Gov. Jim Hunt will ask the General Assembly to cut $600 million from state programs over four years to fund teacher pay raises and expand preschool programs, News & Observer reported Thursday.
The cuts would represent six percent of the state's $10 billion general fund and would almost certainly require cuts of several hundred state jobs, the newspaper said.

The Democratic governor told the newspaper that cutting $150 million a year for the next four years would enable him to keep his campaign pledge to raise teacher salaries to natinal levels and expand the Smart Start childhood program to all 100 counties. North Carolina ranks 42nd nationally in teacher pay.
Hunt is scheduled to release his budget for the next two years when the General Assembly convenes Jan 29.
The legislature has made significant spending cuts in recent years, including $183 million last year.
